name: Papua New Guinean Sign Language
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Reed, Lauren W. 2019. Sign Languages of Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea, and their Challenges for Sign Language Typology. MA thesis, Australian National University, 167 pp. hdl:1885/165444
sources.note: Nothing on PNGSL stress or prosody. PNGSL appears only in passing: fn. 5 says its lexicon is based on the imported 'Melanesian Sign Language' (a reproduction of Australasian Signed English) so many PNGSL signs are non-iconic; one consultant (Delfina, §4-2.12, p. 52) signs PNGSL; refers readers to Reed & Rumsey (in press). The thesis's own phonology remarks (Table 1, Appendix C) concern Kakuyl's rural SL, not PNGSL.

sources.citation: Juhonewe Simonsson, Foreting & Nathalie. 2015. ISO 639-3 Change Request 2015-066: create [pgz] Papua New Guinean Sign Language. SIL International, 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic/administrative only (PNGSL ~50% mutually intelligible with Auslan, first-hand knowledge of the requesters, no published sources cited).

sources.citation: Juhonewe Simonsson, Foreting & Nathalie. 2015. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3 (pgz). SIL International, 4 pp.
sources.note: Nothing; names (PNGSL; 'Melanesian Sign Language' rejected as a hearing-coined name), ~30,000 users, influenced by Auslan and Tok Pisin, official language since May 2015; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.1 languoid page papu1255; Wikipedia 'Papua New Guinean Sign Language'
sources.note: Nothing; both are sociolinguistic/classificatory (BANZSL-related; Kendon 1980 and Rarrick 2020 cited there concern other, unrelated PNG sign languages: Enga and Sinasina).
